items.text: Says the tax-funded health service will always stay free of charge at the point of use, while its leader has repeatedly said the way that service is funded should be re-examined and has been open to other funding models.
Pledged to keep the rule that raises the public pension every year by the highest of prices, wages, or 2.5 percent, and said it would pay for that rule by cutting working-age benefits.

Five of its eight legislators voted against, and two voted for,

items.text: Announced a plan to abolish the main disability benefit and the health-related supplement to the main benefit for working-age adults, replacing them with a regularly reviewed allowance for the most severely ill and locally run support accounts, in order to reduce benefit spending. By its own figures, about 57 percent of the people now receiving those payments would have them changed or withdrawn.
Its deputy leader introduced a bill to limit the main working-age benefit to citizens. About 15 percent of recipients are not citizens, by official figures.
